drawdown_context: CCS entered the cutoff window at 55.71 USD after a -47.8 percent drawdown from its trailing 52-week high. The 10-K (filed 1/30/2025) reported a banner FY24: net income 333.8M (+28.8 percent YoY), revenue 4.40B (+19.1 percent), homebuilding gross margin 23.5 percent (+180 bps), 11,007 home deliveries (+15 percent), buyback step-up, and a 13 percent dividend raise. However, the pre-cutoff Q1 2025 10-Q (filed 4/24/2025) inflected sharply: net income 39.4M (-38.8 percent YoY), EPS 1.26 (-37 percent), gross margin 19.9 percent (-140 bps), new contracts -6.1 percent, backlog -20.9 percent YoY by units / -21.9 percent by dollars, driven by rising rate-buydown incentives in the entry-level Century Complete segment. The drawdown reflects this Q1 inflection plus broader homebuilder de-rating around tariff/rate uncertainty rather than disclosed distress.

rfm_tuples.R: [10-K FY24 P&L] Total revenues 4,398,288 vs 3,692,185 (+19.1%); Net income 333,816 vs 259,224 (+28.8%); Diluted EPS 10.40 vs 8.05 (+29.2%). Homebuilding gross margin 23.5% vs 21.7% (+180 bps).
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: existence check on FY24 strength claim. Does the cleaned 10-K P&L confirm the growth narrative, and does the Q1 2025 10-Q confirm a continuation or an inflection?
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY24 P&L confirmed exactly. BUT the Q1 2025 10-Q (pre-cutoff): net income 39.4M vs 64.3M (-38.8%), EPS 1.26 vs 2.00 (-37.0%), homebuilding gross margin 19.9% vs 21.3% (-140 bps), net new contracts -6.1%, backlog units 1,258 vs 1,590 (-20.9%), backlog 521.1M vs 667.2M (-21.9%). Q1 deliveries essentially flat (2,284 vs 2,358, -3.1%) but backlog and order intake collapsed.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A confirms the 10-K claim but Mode B claim-evolution check between the 10-K and the Q1 10-Q shows the FY24 narrative did NOT hold for one quarter. The inflection is honestly disclosed (-37% EPS, -21% backlog explicitly stated), so this is underperformance against the FY24 trend, not concealment.

rfm_tuples.R: [10-K MD&A overview] 'incentive offerings... including discounts on base home prices, lot premiums, options and upgrades, and financing incentives.' [Q1 10-Q MD&A overview evolved to:] 'incentive offerings... including financing incentives, including interest rate buydowns.' [Q1 10-Q West segment] gross margin 22.1% -230 bps 'primarily driven by higher incentives in the current year period.'
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: claim_evolution between 10-K and Q1 10-Q. The strongest 'distress' tell for an entry-level homebuilder is escalating mortgage rate buy-downs cannibalizing gross margin, particularly when management narrative ADDS the word 'buydowns' to a quarter where margin compresses.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Cross-filing diff (10-K Item 7 MD&A overview vs Q1 2025 10-Q Item 2 MD&A overview + segment commentary)
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K MD&A overview omitted 'buydowns' language entirely. Q1 2025 10-Q ADDED 'interest rate buydowns' to the incentive description AND quantified the margin hit segment-by-segment (West -230 bps, Mountain decline). Net: buy-down language is a NEW disclosure in Q1 2025, and the company tied it directly to margin compression.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catches the most important real-time signal: rate-buydown incentive intensity escalated enough between Jan (10-K) and April (10-Q) that management had to add new language. Honest disclosure of a sector-specific stress (entry-level builders cannot pass through rates), but it is also real economic deterioration in the gross margin engine.

rfm_tuples.R: [10-K Item 5 Q4 2024 monthly:] October 0; November 97,489 at 85.99; December 278,346 at 80.15 (Q4 total 375,835 at 81.66). [Q1 2025 10-Q monthly:] January 0; February 533,720 at 75.77; March 219,617 at 68.85 (Q1 total 753,337 at 73.76). FY24 total: 1.0M shares at ~83.8M. Q1 2025: 55.6M; 3.9M shares remained available at 3/31/2025.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: capital_allocation_tell. Test for the MGPI-style buyback-acceleration-into-trough pattern (the strongest historical 'lying' signal) by tracing month-by-month repurchase pace vs the share price trajectory.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 5 Issuer Purchases + Q1 2025 10-Q Item 2 Issuer Purchases
rfm_tuples.M_value: Buyback dollar pace accelerated 3.5x YoY: Q1 2025 55.6M (753K sh at 73.76) vs Q1 2024 16.1M (187K sh at 86.16). Monthly Q1 2025 trajectory: 0 in Jan, 533K in Feb at 75.77, 220K in March at 68.85 -- they bought MORE shares as the price FELL. By cutoff (5/15/2025) the share price was 55.71, BELOW the Q1 weighted avg of 73.76. Board also upsized revolver to 1.0B on 4/22/2025, and revolver outstanding rose to 237.0M from 135.5M during Q1, partly funding buyback.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B borderline-MGPI pattern: management leveraged the balance sheet (revolver 135.5M -> 237M, +1.0B capacity announced) to ACCELERATE buybacks 3.5x YoY into a falling tape during the same quarter their backlog collapsed -20.9% and gross margin contracted 140 bps. Textbook 'defend the price' tell. Mitigant: Director Ramirez open-market purchased shares on 4/28-5/12 at 53.86-55.74 (see C4) -- honest skin-in-the-game. Net: yellow flag, not red.

rfm_tuples.R: [Q1 2025 10-Q Item 5:] 'During the three months ended March 31, 2025, none of our directors or officers... adopted or terminated a Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangement.' [Form 4 #0001576940-25-000047, Ramirez Elisa Z, Director:] Open market PURCHASES 1,500 sh on 4/28/2025 at 53.86; 500 + 500 sh on 5/9 at 54.68; 400 sh on 5/12 at 55.74.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: insider_vs_calendar. Test (a) for clustered 10b5-1 amendments at the disclosure catalyst (MGPI tell), (b) for the inverse signal: insider open-market BUYING during the same drawdown.
rfm_tuples.M_value: ZERO 10b5-1 plan adoptions/modifications/terminations in Q1 2025 or Q4 2024 -- not the MGPI clustered-amendment pattern. Feb 2025 Francescon brothers (CEO + Executive Chairman) Form 4s show PSU grants (Code A) and tax-withholding share surrenders (Code F at 76.83), NOT open-market sales. CFO Dixon Form 4s are RSU vesting only. Most importantly, Director Ramirez BOUGHT shares on the open market across late April and early May 2025 (purchase prices 53.86-55.74, AT or near the cutoff price of 55.71).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catches the inverse-MGPI signal: no insider flight, no 10b5-1 amendments, and an independent director open-market BUYING into the drawdown. Anti-correlated with the historical short-tell pattern and materially de-risks the buyback-acceleration concern (C3).

rfm_tuples.R: [10-K and Q1 10-Q] 'We were in compliance with all such covenants and requirements under the agreements governing our revolving line of credit, mortgage repurchase facilities, and construction loan agreements.' [Q1 10-Q:] 237.0M outstanding on revolver vs 135.5M at YE24. 'On April 22, 2025, in accordance with the terms of the Credit Agreement, we increased our revolving line of credit to 1.0 billion.'
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A + B: covenant_status + debt evolution. (A) Are they in compliance? (B) Why did they need to upsize the revolver to 1.0B in late April 2025?
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Note 11 Debt + Q1 2025 10-Q Note + balance sheet
rfm_tuples.M_value: Compliance language is hard and repeated in both filings. Revolver upsized to 1.0B on 4/22/2025 -- an EXPANSION of capacity per the Nov 1, 2024 Credit Agreement accordion (provides for up to 3 expansion exercises), NOT a relief amendment. Net homebuilding debt/net capital was 27.4% at YE24, 30.1% at Q1 2025. Mortgage warehouse 232.8M -> 204.3M (down). Senior notes 2027 + 2029; no near-term maturity wall.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A: compliance confirmed. Mode B: revolver upsize is a planned accordion exercise, not distressed amendment. Leverage is rising (27.4% -> 30.1%) but well within investment-grade-like homebuilder norms.

rfm_tuples.R: [10-K Item 5 + Q1 10-Q Item 2:] Quarterly cash dividend 0.23 in 2023, raised to 0.26 in 2024, raised AGAIN to 0.29 on Feb 5, 2025 -- 'a 12% increase from the 0.26 per share quarterly dividend.' 'We expect to continue paying our quarterly cash dividends to stockholders for the remainder of 2025.'
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: dividend_signal as a board-level legal commitment that is hard to send if material adverse trends are known.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 5 dividend table + Q1 2025 10-Q dividend table
rfm_tuples.M_value: Dividend trajectory: 0.23 (2023) -> 0.26 (2024) -> 0.29 (Q1 2025) = +26% over the 2-year window with two distinct raises. The Feb 5, 2025 raise was declared AFTER management had observed YE24 backlog -20.6% YoY. No cut/freeze language in the remainder-of-2025 commentary.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: dividend RAISED 12% in Q1 2025 at the same time gross margin compressed 140 bps and backlog fell 21%. Genuine honesty-alpha: Board signaling durability of cash flow. Anti-correlated with distress.

rfm_tuples.R: [10-K Item 9A:] 'audited by Ernst & Young LLP... /s/ Ernst & Young LLP Denver, Colorado January 29, 2025... We have served as the Company's auditor since 2013.' No Item 9 Changes/Disagreements; ICFR effective; no Item 4.01 8-K.

rfm_tuples.M_value: Ernst & Young (Big 4) since 2013 = 12-year continuous tenure. Clean opinion on financials and ICFR. No 8-K Item 4.01 events in EDGAR pre-cutoff. CAM is community-level impairment judgment; no exception found.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Auditor history is clean and stable. CAM is on the correct sensitivity (inventory impairment) but produced no exception, consistent with small 8.8M FY24 inventory impairment booked.

rfm_tuples.R: [10-K Item 7:] 'wholly-owned subsidiaries, Inspire Home Loans Inc., Parkway Title, LLC, IHL Home Insurance Agency, LLC, and IHL Escrow Inc., which provide mortgage, title, insurance brokerage and escrow services... primarily to our homebuyers.' [10-K Note 11:] 232.8M outstanding under mortgage warehouse facilities (425M capacity). [Q1 10-Q:] 204.3M / 375M capacity, weighted avg 6.0%, all maturities through 11/14/2025.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: captive-mortgage concentration tell. Entry-level homebuilders run a captive Inspire-style mortgage subsidiary; quantify the dependency and the refinancing wall.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Inspire mortgage operations essentially CCS-customer-only (financial services revenue 92.9M in FY24 = 2.1% of total revenue; mortgages originated +29.9% YoY in FY24). Warehouse capacity REDUCED from 425M to 375M between 12/31/24 and 3/31/25 (banks pulled 50M of uncommitted capacity). All warehouse maturities short-dated (through 11/14/2025), creating H2 2025 refinancing wall. Q1 financial services income before tax fell to 2.4M.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B sector-specific yellow flag: warehouse capacity cut 50M (12%) and Financial Services earnings collapsed YoY in Q1. The November 2025 warehouse-renewal wall is the most likely 'next disclosure surprise' for CCS. Not red because facilities are uncommitted/customary and the captive subsidy to homebuying volumes matters more.

rfm_tuples.R: [10-K + Q1 10-Q] 'Our utilization of land option contracts is dependent on... availability of land sellers willing to enter into option takedown arrangements.' [10-K:] 80,632 lots owned and controlled at YE24 (44.3% owned / 55.7% controlled, up from 41.5% owned in 2023). [Q1 10-Q:] 79,014 lots at 3/31/2025. Non-refundable cash deposits on land options: 54.7M at YE24 vs 18.3M at YE23 (+199%).
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: land-bank / JV opacity sector-specific tell. Quantify the option-deposit ladder and ownership creep.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 1 + Note on VIE / land options + Q1 10-Q narrative
rfm_tuples.M_value: Owned-vs-controlled ratio shifted from 41.5%/58.5% owned at YE23 to 44.3%/55.7% at YE24 = management TOOK ON 2.8 ppts more direct land risk during the deceleration. Non-refundable deposits TRIPLED (18.3M -> 54.7M). Lot count drifted down 80,632 -> 79,014 (-2%) in Q1, modest pipeline trimming.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B sector tell: rotating from off-balance-sheet land control to ON-balance-sheet land ownership at the EXACT moment the market is slowing -- consuming working capital. Non-refundable deposits tripling is worth watching. Not red because absolute land at risk is modest vs 2.6B equity.

Mode B: no hidden community-level write-downs lurking; the small Q1 impairment suggests the lever is being used conservatively, not for a kitchen-sink quarter.

summary: CCS is the canonical 'honest about the inflection' homebuilder: a banner FY24 (net income +29%, gross margin +180 bps, dividend raised twice) followed by a brutally honest Q1 2025 10-Q that volunteered the slowdown (-37% EPS, -21% backlog, -140 bps gross margin, NEW 'interest rate buydowns' language in MD&A, segment-by-segment margin attribution). The framework's strongest Mode B tells RESOLVE the pressure rather than amplify it: (1) Dividend RAISED 12% to 0.29 on Feb 5, 2025 AFTER management saw YE24 backlog -20.6% -- legally binding signal of cash flow durability; (2) ZERO 10b5-1 amendments in Q4 2024 or Q1 2025 (anti-MGPI); (3) Independent Director Elisa Ramirez open-market PURCHASED 2,900 shares on 4/28-5/12/2025 at 53.86-55.74 (at the cutoff level of 55.71) -- inverse-MGPI buying into the drawdown; (4) Ernst & Young (Big 4) since 2013, clean ICFR, no Item 9 disagreements; (5) Founder-led with no governance transitions; (6) Revolver upsize to 1.0B on 4/22/2025 is an accordion exercise, NOT a relief amendment, and they are in compliance with all covenants. The real yellow flags are sector-specific and forward-looking, not lying tells: buyback pace tripled YoY (55.6M Q1 vs 16.1M prior) while funded by a revolver draw (135.5M -> 237M) and gross margin compressed -- this borders the buyback-defense pattern but is materially mitigated by the director open-market buying. Captive mortgage warehouse capacity was cut 12% (425M -> 375M, all maturities Nov 2025) creating an H2 refinancing wall. Land-bank deposits tripled to 54.7M and owned ratio rose 41.5% -> 44.3%, taking on more direct land risk into a softening cycle. Net: a real cyclical earnings cut is in flight, but management is signaling truthfully via dividend, director buying, and proactive Q1 disclosure of buydown intensity. Composite lands in the NEUTRAL band (~0.30-0.40) -- yellow on capital allocation and captive-mortgage capacity but not a SHORT-tier candidate. Forward return -6.7% is consistent with NEUTRAL.
